newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dec qtr GDP growth at top of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NZ Dec qtr GDP growth at top of forecasts.

text.p: Data on Thursday showed New Zealand December quarter Gross Domestic Product growth at the top end of market expectations, at 0.7 percent.
The median forecast from economists was for 0.4 percent growth, with the forecasts ranging from 0.3 to 0.7 percent.
The rise follows a 0.8 percent increase for the September quarter, revised up from 0.6 percent.
For the year ended December, actual economic growth was 2.7 percent, following a 3.5 percent rise in the year to December 1995.
Statistics New Zealand said the economy was now 2.9 percent higher than in the December 1995 quarter on a seasonally adjusted basis.
"Over the last four quarters the economy appears to have settled into a steady growth pattern of between 2.5 to 3.5 percent per annum," SNZ said.
Internal demand fell by 0.7 percent in the quarter.
Investment in fixed assets, excluding residential buildings, fell 4.5 percent in the quarter following a rise of 1.6 percent in the September quarter.

SNZ said the latest quarter's results were influenced by the inclusion of an oil tanker used at the Maui-B rig, which was imported in the September quarter. When this was excluded, business investment fell 1.3 percent in the December quarter and 1.7 percent in the previous quarter.
The December quarter fall in investment occurred in all major asset types.
Domestic economic activity was maintained by a 2.1 percent quarterly rise in exports and a 1.6 percent fall in imports.

Exports are now 6.3 percent higher than in the December 1995 quarter. SNZ said while much of the annual growth could be attributed to record dairy product exports, manufactured exports had continued to grow despite the high exchange rate.

Household expenditure recovered slightly to rise 0.4 percent in the December quarter. SNZ said it showed little sign of resurgence in response to the July 1996 tax cuts and Christmas spending and was basically flat, following a fall of 0.7 percent in the September quarter.

The largest contributions to the 0.7 percent rise in quarterly GDP were made by transport, communications and manufacturing. There was a recovery in agriculture, but falls were seen in forestry, mining, personal and community services.
Expenditure-based GDP rose 0.6 percent in the quarter, against a 0.8 percent rise in the September quarter.
The GDP implicit price deflator, a broad measure of the overall price change for final goods and services produced in New Zealand, rose 1.6 percent in the December year.
